text:
Brightline Ops: FYI we started seeing TLS failures on our VPC endpoints after last night's rotation. Apps report handshake errors.

Emily (Customer Ops): Error samples from their app: `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`, and occasional `tls: handshake failure`. They say the hosted endpoint OK, only VPC failing.

Alex S: Can you paste a curl/openssl test from inside the VPC? We suspect chain/sni/cache.

Brightline Ops: Ran curl from an app host:
````
curl -v https://inference.vpc.brightline.internal:443
* Connected to inference.vpc.brightline.internal (10.20.30.40) port 443
* SSL peer certificate:
* subject: CN=redwood-inference
* start date: Jan  1 00:00:00 2026 GMT
* expire date: Apr  1 00:00:00 2026 GMT
* SSL: certificate subject name 'redwood-inference' does not match target host name 'inference.vpc.brightline.internal'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject name 'redwood-inference' does not match target host name
````

Jordan: Two quick things to triage: 1) missing intermediate(s) in the served chain; 2) SNI mismatch — their LB may be sending a different server_name (or using default cert). Also note HAProxy caches certs until process reload in some configs.

Maya: Also check OCSP/CRL egress — if CA intermediate changed, validation may attempt OCSP and fail if outbound is blocked. Customer firewall shows some dropped egress to `ocsp.digicert.com`.

Sam: Ask them to run this from inside the VPC and paste full output: 
````
openssl s_client -connect inference.vpc.brightline.internal:443 -showcerts -servername inference.vpc.brightline.internal
````
We need to inspect the chain order and SANs.

Brightline Ops: Posted openssl output. Chain shows only two certs: leaf and root; intermediate missing. Snippet: 
````
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=redwood-inference
   i:/CN=Redwood Intermediate CA
 1 s:/CN=Redwood Root CA
   i:/CN=Redwood Root CA
````

Alex S: Missing intermediate is likely the cause. Some TLS clients will fail if the server doesn't present the full chain. Why did rotator drop it?

cert-rotator-bot: Rotation job 9271 status: SUCCESS (bundle_size=2 certs). Uploaded bundle hash abc123.

Jordan: That suggests the uploaded bundle contained leaf+root but not intermediate. Hypothesis: the customer LB requires leaf+intermediate+root concatenated in a single PEM in that order. If our rotator mis-parsed their chained PEM or the intermediate was omitted during bundle creation, HAProxy would serve an incomplete chain.

Maya: Short-term mitigation: re-upload corrected PEM containing leaf + intermediate + root, then ask customer to reload/restart HAProxy so it picks up the new chain (some versions cache until restart). If they cannot restart, look for cert-cache clearing options.

Alex S: Also ask them to `curl` with `--resolve` to force SNI/host resolution and confirm: `curl -v --resolve inference.vpc.brightline.internal:443:10.20.30.40 https://inference.vpc.brightline.internal/health`

Brightline Ops: Willing to do a 15-min window for restart. They provided intermediate fingerprint `SHA1: AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:...`

Jordan: I pulled customer 9271 cert records — we do have the intermediate in our store. I'll assemble a concatenated PEM (leaf + intermediate + root) and push it as a hotfix bundle. @Maya can you kick the rotation?

Maya: Pushing hotfix bundle now.

cert-rotator-bot: Rotation job 9271-hotfix started. user=maya; upload=certchain_fix.pem

cert-rotator-bot: Rotation job 9271-hotfix completed: SUCCESS. New bundle includes 3 certs in order: leaf, intermediate, root. hash=def456.

Maya: Please restart/reload HAProxy during your maintenance window and re-run the openssl test.

Brightline Ops: HAProxy reloaded. New openssl output shows intermediate present. They also ran the curl `--resolve` health check and got HTTP/200. App logs show no further handshake errors.

Alex S: Great, marking customer incident resolved. Action items for us: 1) file infra ticket to add rotator validation to ensure intermediate presence (ENG-1952), 2) add a post-rotation check that fetches `openssl s_client` from a probe host to verify chain, 3) publish KB note advising customers to allow OCSP/CRL egress for CA endpoints.

Jordan: Filed ENG-1952 in infra backlog: "rotator: validate chain completeness and PEM ordering".

Sam: Recommend security advisory for customers on OCSP egress and SNI correctness.

Emily (Customer Ops): Closing loop with Brightline and attaching remediation steps to ticket. Brightline confirmed fixes and thanked team. :thumbsup:
